selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer matches the advertiser's focus on fitness, high willingness to pay premium prices, and science-backed nutritional claims, aligning closely with Pantrygood's audience of clean-ingredient and wellness seekers.

The Busy Parent embodies the subscription-based, convenience-first food delivery buyer who naturally shops on Kitchenly, matching the time-saving needs of upper-class households looking for nutritious meals.
The Sustainability Buyer strongly overlaps with vegan food delivery and Pantrygood's values-driven audience, responding well to ethical sourcing, organic footprints, and supply chain transparency.
The Fitness Enthusiast directly targets the advertiser's workout and protein-rich product focus, connecting performance-oriented goals with premium meal subscriptions.

rejected.reason: The Gen Z Aesthete has a lower AOV of $48 and focuses heavily on trends and beauty/fashion rather than high-end fitness subscriptions.
The Pet Parent focuses entirely on animal care rather than human fitness-oriented food delivery apps.
The Affluent Classic prefers traditional home goods, classic apparel, and travel rather than fitness-centric food delivery apps.
The Convenience-First Millennial is too heavily skewed toward low brand loyalty and quick impulse commerce rather than premium science-backed fitness nutrition.
The Value-Conscious Shopper seeks discount-forward bundles and low-end deals, which contradicts the advertiser's premium price tier and high AOV strategy.
The Gifter is explicitly disinterested in subscription-only models, which directly conflicts with the advertiser's subscription business model.
